prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moiré flat-band matter.

statement.case_for: After reading the other ballots I move my first choice from B009 to B021. Twisted bilayer graphene is a case where a simple, analytically transparent mechanism (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model: interlayer tunnelling competing with the Dirac velocity gives a magic angle where the bands flatten) was written down in 2011 and then confirmed by experiment in 2018 with correlated insulators and superconductivity. That is the prediction-then-observation chain I trust most. The idea has spread far beyond one material, to other moiré systems, fractional Chern insulators and tunable correlated matter, and it has been reproduced by many independent groups. Theory plus experiment (MacDonald and Bistritzer with Jarillo-Herrero) is also a clean attribution that fits the three-person limit. Among the condensed-matter and theory candidates it combines first-place support (Eriksson-Olle) with top-three support (Olsson-Eva), and it is the candidate I rank highly that colleagues also rank highly.
statement.case_against: The field is only about eight years old and the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still unsettled, so part of the headline claim is not yet understood. That matters to me, because I care whether a breakthrough is understood and not only whether it works. The experimental credit is also narrow: Cao and co-authors, and the parallel Dean-group and Yacoby/Young work, cannot be represented in the supplied names, and Bistritzer's share relative to MacDonald is a real question. I also dropped B009 because it had no support beyond my own ballot and the physics versus biology boundary is a serious obstacle, even though I still think it is a good physics idea.

responses.point: Eriksson-Olle ranks B021 first as a clean pairing of the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction with the Jarillo-Herrero experiments, treats confirmation by many groups as robust despite the open pairing question, and ranks B019 (DMFT) third while worrying that it is theory-only with no single decisive experimental test.
responses.response: I agree on the structure of the B021 claim, and I accept that the discovery of correlated phases is robust even if the pairing mechanism is not; that is why I now put it first. I only partly share the worry about DMFT. Its content is a controlled mechanism (exact in infinite dimensions, with the impurity mapping), and the Mott physics has been checked in photoemission and in cold-atom experiments, so I would not rule out a method prize. But I accept that it is a harder sell as a discovery than B021, and Metzner's absence from the credited names is a real problem, so I keep B019 only as an alternative.

responses.point: Olsson-Eva ranks B021 second, calls recognition slightly early but defensible, and stresses that the Jarillo-Herrero 2018 experiments are the original observation, while noting that the Cao and Fatemi co-authors and the parallel Dean, Yacoby and Young experiments complicate who did what first.
responses.response: I take the 'slightly early' remark seriously, since my own opening ballot put B021 sixth for that reason. My answer is that the central claim, flat bands and correlated phases at the magic angle, has already been reproduced across transport, scanning probes and spectroscopy, whereas the open question is the superconducting pairing, which is a follow-up and not the discovery. I agree on the attribution problem for the experimental side. I would keep the credited names as supplied, tie the citation to the prediction and the observation of correlated phases, and let the committee record the co-authors' contributions in its scientific background.

responses.point: Kroll-Stefan ranks B024 (optical lattice clocks) first as a measurement instrument whose precision redefines what can be measured, and ranks B020 third while asking whether a still-maturing simulation programme is premature compared with more finished results.
responses.response: I respect the maturity and the confirmation by independent laboratories behind B024, and I agree that B020 is still unfinished, especially for fermions, which was my reason for ranking it eighth. My reservation on B024 is not about quality but about kind: it follows the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize closely, so the novelty is a refinement of a prize-honoured technology, and the fundamental-physics yield so far is limits and not a discovery. I would not oppose it, and I regard it as the main competitor, but I find B021 the more original new mechanism.

responses.point: Lindroth-Eva ranks B047 (Aharonov-Bohm and Berry phases) seventh, calling it late rather than premature but noting that a committee may judge the effects as already honoured indirectly through the topological prizes, and ranks B020 first.
responses.response: I disagree with discounting B047 on that basis. The 2016 prize honoured topological phase transitions and phases of matter, and a prize for an application of a concept does not credit its source. Aharonov-Bohm and Berry phases are the root of Hall quantisation, polarisation theory and molecular geometric phases, and Berry is alive and can be named. I do agree it is two separate discoveries, with Bohm deceased and priority questions on Ehrenberg-Siday and Pancharatnam, so I cannot put it ahead of the more broadly supported candidates, but I keep it as my first alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene makes a 2026 award premature relative to B024 or B020.
How to treat the experimental co-authors (Cao and others) and the parallel experimental groups when only Jarillo-Herrero can be named.
Whether the committee wants to split Bistritzer and MacDonald credit or prefers a two-person B021 prize, as Danielsson-Ulf proposed.
Whether B009 or B047 could be handled as a second prize part without exceeding three people in total; at present I think not.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B021 or the alternatives. I know none of the credited names as collaborators. I work in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Johansson-Goran and Olsson-Eva (Chalmers), but I have no specific collaboration with them, and Johansson-Goran's declared closeness to circuit QED (B002) does not touch my proposal.
